rv.q: Sorry to disabuse you, but no such luck – and not only because musical arranger Adam Morris gives the songs such maudlin settings.

Poet has done an excellent job of dramatising the book, filleting it into a fleet two-and-half-hours and finessing its romantic shenanigans intelligibly, while maintaining the wit and wisdom of Austen’s original.
If the tone of Poet and Nichols’ show more resembles Elinor than Marianne, in terms of its romantic rites of passage, it nevertheless remains a merry dance of a show.

cn.t: This Austen adaptation receives mixed reviews, with critics finding it enjoyable but uneven. Pop songs and knockabout humor add irreverence, though some feel the staging lacks shape and emotional depth.
